messages.content: help me write a card to my grandmother. i want to say that i like our time together, but i do not want a long message.
i love our time together. i am happy when i visit you, and i hope to see you again soon.
we cook together. can you make it about that?
then keep it about cooking: i love our time together in the kitchen. thank you for cooking with me.
i want to say that i learn from her, too.
i love our time together in the kitchen. thank you for cooking with me and teaching me new things.
can you make the whole card sound like it comes from a child?
i love cooking with you. you teach me new things, and i am happy when we are together.
should i say that the card is for a holiday?
say that if the card is for a holiday. you have not said what the card is for, so that detail does not need to be in the message yet.
it is just a card because i miss her.
then you could end with: i miss you and hope to see you soon.
i went to a shop yesterday and again today. yesterday it was closed. today it was open. can both of those be true?
yes. the shop can be closed on one visit and open on another. your sentences are about different visits, so they do not say opposite things about the same moment.
write two sentences from only what i told you.
yesterday, i went to the shop and found it closed. today, i went again and found it open.
did you add anything about buying something?
no. the two sentences say when you went and whether the shop was open. they do not say what you did after finding it open.
can you add a made up next part now?
today, i went inside and asked a worker about a book in the window. she brought it to the desk so i could look at it. i read the first page before choosing whether to buy it.
did i buy it in that next part?
not yet. you looked at it and read the first page, but the story stops before you choose.
my friend always chooses the same game. i like being with them, but i want to try a different game today.
you can say both things clearly: i like playing with you. could we try a different game today?
i do not want them to think i hate their game.
then add that you still like it: i like our game, but i would enjoy trying something different today. could we choose another one together?
what if they ask which one?
if you have a game in mind, name it. if you do not, ask whether you can both think of a few choices and choose one together.
i want to ask them for a choice, too.
you could say: i have one idea. what would you like to try? then we can choose between them.
is it okay to like a game and not want to play it every day?
yes. you can like something without choosing it every day. you can enjoy the old game and still want a different kind of afternoon.
change this to i: she walked to school and gave her teacher a note. then she sat near the window and opened her book.
i walked to school and gave my teacher a note. then i sat near the window and opened my book.
now change it to we, with one teacher and a book for each person.
we walked to school and gave our teacher a note. then we sat near the window and each opened a book.
why did you not write we opened our book?
you said that each person has a book. each opened a book makes that detail clear. our book could sound like one book used by the whole group.
now let the group use just one book together.
we walked to school and gave our teacher a note. then we sat near the window and opened one book to read together.
was there one note or a note for each person?
the sentences say a note, so they are about one note given to the teacher. you did not ask to change that part.
make the note a letter instead, and keep the group with one book.
we walked to school and gave our teacher a letter. then we sat near the window and opened one book to read together.
someone asked if i wanted cake after lunch. i said i would like some later. did i say i do not like cake?
no. you said you would like some later. that can mean you want cake, but not at that moment.
i was full. help me say that without a long explanation.
thank you. i am full now, but i would like some later.
what if they say i should have told them before they cut it?
you could say: i am sorry. i did not know you were about to cut it. could we keep my piece for later?
i did know they were about to cut it. do not say i did not know.
then keep that out: i am sorry i did not say it before. could we keep my piece for later?
can you write it without saying sorry?
thank you for the cake. could we keep my piece for later? i am full right now.
what is the request in that message?
you are asking to keep your piece of cake so you can have it later.
write three sentences about a person waiting for rain to stop. use now in the first one.
now she is waiting for the rain to stop. she looks through the window and holds her book. she wants to read in the garden when the rain is over.
put it all in the past.
she was waiting for the rain to stop. she looked through the window and held her book. she wanted to read in the garden when the rain was over.
does the past story say she finally read outside?
no. it says what she wanted to do. it does not say whether the rain stopped or whether she went into the garden.
add a last sentence that makes it clear she stayed inside.
the rain went on, so she stayed inside and read on the sofa instead.
now write the whole past story with that last sentence.

she was waiting for the rain to stop. she looked through the window and held her book. she wanted to read in the garden when the rain was over. the rain went on, so she stayed inside and read on the sofa instead.
i made tea in a room where other people work. i want to leave the cup until later, but someone else may need it.
you could wash it after your tea and put it back, so another person can use it. if you need to leave right away, ask whether you can keep it until you return.
i can wash it now. i just keep putting small things off.
then this can be one small thing to finish now. wash the cup, put it back, and you will not need to remember it later.
can you make that into a short note for myself?
wash the cup and put it back before leaving the room.
what if it is my own cup?
then the needs of another person may not be the reason to wash it. you can still choose to clean it before leaving so it is ready when you want it again.
write the note so it works whether the cup is mine or not.
wash the cup before leaving, then put it in the right place.
that sounds simple enough.
yes. it gives you one clear task to finish before you go.
i see the word read in i read every day and i read yesterday. is it written the same?
yes. read is written the same in both sentences, but the sound is different. every day gives the first sentence its meaning, and yesterday puts the other in the past.
can you give a different sentence where yesterday makes the time clear?
yesterday, i read a book in the library.
now make a sentence about a plan for tomorrow.
tomorrow, i will read a book in the library.
does will read use a new written word for read?
no. will gives information about the plan, while the written word read does not change.
write a short conversation with these ideas.
did you read yesterday? yes, i read at the library. will you read tomorrow too? yes, i will read there again after lunch.
what does there mean in the last answer?
there is about the library in that answer, because the library was the place given before.
a small object is behind a picture on my desk. from my chair, i cannot see it. does that mean it is gone?
no. if you cannot see it from your chair, that does not mean it is gone. the picture may be between you and the object.
what could i do to check without moving the object itself?
you could look from another side of the desk or move the picture. that may let you see the object without moving it.
i moved the picture and saw it. help me write what happened.
i could not see the object because it was behind a picture. when i moved the picture, i could see the object on the desk.
can i say the object came there when i moved the picture?
not if it was there before. moving the picture changed what you could see. it did not bring the object to the desk.
use only simple words for that last explanation.
say: the object was already there. moving the picture let me see it.
i chose a book because i thought it was short. then i found more pages at the back. is it wrong to choose another book?
no. you learned something new about the book. you can use that information to change your choice if you need something short today.
i still like the story. i only need a short book for a school task.
then you can keep the longer story for another time and choose a short book for the task. those are different reasons for reading, and one book does not have to meet both needs.
write a message to my teacher asking whether this longer book is still okay.
i found that my book is longer than i thought. is it still okay for this task, or should i choose a shorter one?
should i say that the teacher gave me the wrong book?
not unless that happened. you said that you chose the book. the message can ask about the task without saying the teacher did something wrong.
keep the question but make it shorter.
my book is longer than i thought. is it still okay for this task?
hello. i am sitting in a garden and wanted a little conversation.
hello. what can you see from where you are sitting?
a tree, a table, and two people reading. it is a quiet place.
that sounds like a place where you can take your time. are you there to read too, or just to sit for a while?
just to sit. i have been working all morning.
then you have a change from the morning. you can sit without making the time into another task.
can you ask something about the garden rather than my work?
is there a part of the garden you like more than the rest?
ask that with fewer words.
which part of the garden do you like most?
the tree. i like looking up through its leaves.
then the tree gives you something quiet to look at while you rest. you do not need a book to enjoy being there.
my friend brought a book before i asked for it. can i say my question made them bring it?
not if they brought it before you asked. your later question could not be the reason they brought it. however, you might have said something else before today.
i had told them last week that i wanted to read it. i only asked today whether they remembered.
then last week gave them information about what you wanted. today, you asked whether they remembered. those are two different parts of the conversation.
write it as a short story without adding a reason they did not give.
last week, i told my friend that i wanted to read a book. today, they brought it. after they came, i asked whether they remembered our conversation. they already had the book with them.
does the story say they forgot?
no. it says that you asked whether they remembered. asking a question does not make either possible answer true.
write a question i could ask that sounds happy to see the book.
you brought the book! did you remember that i wanted to read it?
write a story where a young child helps her father learn a game, and he listens.

a girl asks her father to play a game she made up. he sits on the floor and asks what he should do first. she puts three small objects in front of him and gives him a rule for moving them. he tries it, but she says that he moved two when he should only move one. he asks her to show him again. this time, he moves one object and waits. she says that he has done it right. they keep playing until she wants to change the rule.
why does he ask her rather than make up his own rule?
it is her game, and he wants to understand how she wants to play. listening gives her room to teach him.
does being a parent mean he already knows the game?
no. the girl made up this game. he can be her father and still need her to explain it.
make the last part a short conversation.
can we change the rule now? yes, but tell me what is changing first. now you move two objects instead of one. okay. show me once, and then i will try.
i want you to answer my next question with only yes or no. can you do that?
yes.
is three more than two?
yes.
now you can use a full sentence. why was the last reply enough?
you asked whether three is more than two and asked for only yes or no. yes answered that question without adding anything else.
explain that in fewer words.
you asked for only yes or no. yes gave the correct answer without adding more words.
now ask me a question that needs more than yes or no to give useful detail.
what do you like to read, and why?
i like stories because they help me think about other people.
you like stories for more than what happens in them. they also give you a way to think about how other people live and feel.
i opened the window to hear the music outside. did i say i wanted to see something?
no. you gave hearing the music as your reason. opening a window might also change what you can see, but you did not say that was what you wanted.
write two sentences about why i opened the window, without adding a feeling.
i opened the window to hear the music outside. i wanted to listen to it from my room.
did that say i heard it before opening the window?
no. it says why you opened the window, but it does not say when you first heard the music.
can you keep it to one sentence instead?
i opened the window to hear the music outside.
now make it into a made up story with a happy person.
a person can hear music from the garden and opens the window to listen. she sees her friend playing a song near the tree. she sits by the window and enjoys the music without leaving her room.
is the friend part of my original sentence?
no. the friend is a new detail added for the made up story.
help me write a note that says my brother should call me after he gets home.
please call me when you get home.
i am writing to my brother, but the note will be read by my mother first. make it clear who should call.
please ask my brother to call me when he gets home.
my mother does not need to ask him. she only needs to give him the note.
please give this note to my brother: call me when you get home.
why does you mean someone different in the two parts?
the first part asks your mother to give the note. the words after that are the message for your brother. that part asks him to call you when he gets home.
explain that with fewer words.
the first part is for your mother. the message about calling is for your brother.
make a note without using you for two different people.
please give this message to my brother. he should call me after he gets home.
